description: Figure 3 is a vertical bar chart titled "Difference in average word error rate (WER) from Whisper large-v3 after cumulative automated optimisation steps," which illustrates the performance gap between two fine-tuned models, NESAC ft model (orange bars) and SESHA ft model (green bars), relative to the Whisper large-v3 baseline. The horizontal axis represents the "Difference in Average WER from Whisper large," scaled linearly from 0.000 to 0.003, with tick marks at intervals of 0.001. The vertical axis lists five cumulative post-processing optimizations applied in sequence: "Normalised," "Add Spacing," "Remove Spacing," "Americanisms," and "Dates." For each optimization step, two bars are shown side-by-side, representing the WER difference for each model. The NESAC ft model consistently shows a higher WER difference than the SESHA ft model for all steps. The values, read from the right end of each bar, are: for "Normalised," NESAC ft model at 0.00334 and SESHA ft model at 0.00323; for "Add Spacing," NESAC ft model at 0.00319 and SESHA ft model at 0.00344; for "Remove Spacing," NESAC ft model at 0.00311 and SESHA ft model at 0.00306; for "Americanisms," NESAC ft model at 0.00299 and SESHA ft model at 0.00302; and for "Dates," NESAC ft model at 0.00257 and SESHA ft model at 0.00228. The bars are grouped by optimization step, with the NESAC ft model bars consistently appearing slightly taller than the SESHA ft model bars in each group, indicating a consistently higher WER difference for the NESAC ft model across all applied optimizations.
